one_line: A local-first personal budget tracker with structured agent access to deterministic financial state.
what_it_does: Records income, expenses, bills, savings, credit, and loans, and exposes validated read/write budget operations to WebMCP agents alongside the normal visual interface.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools and shared deterministic financial state make agent reads and explicit transactions more reliable than UI driving, but a competent browser agent could perform much of the same small-scale budgeting workflow with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies eleven structured WebMCP tools against the same deterministic financial logic.
The frame sheet shows a conventional budget dashboard but no visible agent invocation or shared-state transition.
execution_rationale: The dashboard appears coherent and intentionally designed, but the available video frames mostly repeat an overview screen and do not demonstrate a complete transaction or projection workflow end to end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet visibly shows a polished financial overview with navigation, summary cards, and detailed panels.
Packet describes income, expenses, commitments, credit, loans, and projections, but transcript is absent.
impact_rationale: Personal budgeting is a clear, real need, and a private local-first alternative can provide credible value to users who want simple tracking without subscriptions or bank connections.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies personal budget control and privacy as the target need.
Frame sheet shows a usable money-at-a-glance dashboard.
creativity_rationale: The local-first, deterministic human-and-agent budget design is a thoughtful angle on a familiar category, though the underlying product concept remains conventional.
creativity_evidence: Agent-native access without embedding a chatbot or surrendering financial rules to an AI is a distinctive framing.
Visual product remains a standard budget-tracker paradigm.
usability_note: Clear dashboard structure is visible, though repeated frames provide limited evidence of deeper flows.
standouts: Explicit separation of available cash, credit, and liabilities
advance_reason: Strong practical value and credible WebMCP enhancement, with moderate evidence limits on execution.

one_line: A human-approved browser coding workspace where agents inspect, patch, and verify bounded code changes.
what_it_does: Provides a CodeMirror editor and structured WebMCP tools for file listing, search, digest-checked exact replacements, diff review, and handoff to a constrained coding bridge.
leverage_rationale: Typed file and diff operations with digest checks and human approval materially outperform pixel/keyboard automation for safe, precise code collaboration; the agent is central rather than decorative.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes bounded listings, search results, file digests, exact replacements, and reversible diff review.
Frame sheet shows a real scoped webmcp serve bridge with allowed-root, origin, write, and full-auto policies.
execution_rationale: The editor and bridge workflow appears coherent and operationally intentional, though the frame sheet emphasizes setup and does not visibly show a completed patch approval.
execution_evidence: Frames show terminal bridge configuration and a live production client/editor.
Packet reports an alive demo and describes inspect-to-diff-to-approval flow.
impact_rationale: Safe human-agent code editing addresses a substantial developer need, especially where precise changes, reviewability, and workspace boundaries matter.
impact_evidence: Packet specifies reversible patches, SHA-256 digest matching, and terminal policy controls.
Visible VS Code-style workspace supports the claimed use case.
creativity_rationale: The combination of browser-native tools, digest-guarded edits, reversible review, and a bounded authenticated bridge is an original and ambitious collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Human reviews exact generated diffs before terminal handoff.
Frame captions visibly emphasize the real Ghostty bridge and bounded workspace.
usability_note: Editor-plus-diff workflow is legible; bridge setup may add operational complexity.
red_flags: The video evidence shows bridge setup more clearly than an end-to-end agent patch.
advance_reason: High leverage and strong developer value with unusually concrete safety boundaries.

one_line: An agentic architecture canvas for designing, auditing, and chaos-testing cloud topologies.
what_it_does: Lets humans and agents build a connected architecture graph, run audits, inject outages, and expose topology and audit resources through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Shared graph state and structured topology/audit operations make agent collaboration substantially more precise than asking an agent to emit diagrams or drive a canvas manually.
leverage_evidence: Packet names add_service_node, connect_services, simulate_chaos_outage, run_architecture_audit, and live topology/audit resources.
Frame sheet visibly shows a node-and-edge architecture canvas with configuration panels.
execution_rationale: The visual canvas and stated workflow are coherent, but the frames do not clearly prove an audit, chaos run, or self-healing result completing.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows repeated graph-editor states with connected nodes and side panels.
Demo is reported alive and the packet describes a centralized reducer shared by human and agent actions.
impact_rationale: Architecture design and failure analysis are real engineering problems, and a visual, testable shared canvas could provide credible value to developers and platform teams.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies diagram staleness, inaccessible text diagrams, and inability to test failures as needs.
Visible interface is an architecture workflow rather than a generic chat output.
creativity_rationale: Combining architecture modeling, automated threat analysis, chaos injection, and self-healing in a collaborative WebMCP canvas is a fresh, ambitious synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Concept treats the agent as an active architecture collaborator rather than a text diagram generator.
Node graph, live resources, and chaos operations form a distinctive interaction model.
usability_note: The graph metaphor is recognizable, though small frame text limits assessment of interaction clarity.
red_flags: No readable execution log or self-healing result in the frame sheet.
standouts: Chaos engineering inside the architecture canvas
advance_reason: Ambitious and high-value developer workflow with clear WebMCP relevance.

one_line: A WebMCP environment for agents to iteratively reconstruct and evaluate physical motion.
what_it_does: Frames human-motion reconstruction as a continuous simulation search problem with cheap rollouts, ground-truth comparison, and a dynamic benchmark environment.
leverage_rationale: The product is itself an agent-facing experimental environment: structured repeated simulation and evaluation are impractical to reproduce comparably through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet defines a WebMCP RL environment with repeated simulation and an agent receiving a natural-language prior.
Frame sheet visibly presents a motion reconstruction benchmark and environment framing, though no call log is shown.
execution_rationale: The benchmark concept and visual presentation are coherent, but frames are primarily landing-page/demo states and do not establish a complete agent rollout or evaluation loop.
execution_evidence: Frames show two motion figures and the benchmark/environment messaging.
Packet reports two motion examples but provides no transcript and limited operational detail.
impact_rationale: Researchers and developers need richer, cheaper environments for testing agents and simulators; dynamic physical reconstruction is a credible high-value use case.
impact_evidence: Packet articulates the limitation of static benchmarks and the value of cheap simulation with unambiguous verification.
Visible interface communicates a specific motion-reconstruction task.
creativity_rationale: Replacing static benchmark questions with evolving continuous physics search and motion reconstruction is genuinely novel and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: The benchmark becomes an environment rather than a one-shot answer page.
Concept connects agent evaluation, surrogate modeling, and physical trajectories.
usability_note: The benchmark framing is clear, but the captured UI does not reveal enough of the actual experiment controls.
red_flags: Product-motion evidence is mostly promotional UI and does not show a concrete tool call or completed rollout.
standouts: Continuous search with cheap physical simulation
advance_reason: Exceptional concept and WebMCP fit outweigh thin execution evidence.

one_line: A consent-controlled WebMCP control plane that routes a dinner-and-ride outcome across providers.
what_it_does: Publishes and validates connector capabilities, plans a constrained dinner plus accessible ride, executes only after confirmation, and produces a combined receipt with retry visibility.
leverage_rationale: Cross-site capability discovery, connector validation, shared planning state, human consent, and partial-failure handling are a major structural improvement over generic UI navigation.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes live tool count changing from six to eight, connector publication, planning, provider calls, and a single approval gate.
Frame sheet shows the plan flow and a tool-list-oriented state, though the actual calls are not legible.
execution_rationale: The deterministic demo has a well-defined end-to-end story with connector rejection, safe publication, confirmation, retries, and receipt generation; video evidence shows the product flow but not every result clearly.
execution_evidence: Packet specifies an executable 18-check validator, no-reload tool-count transition, call list, receipt, and ride-only retry.
Frame sheet shows planning and result states for the evening workflow.
impact_rationale: Coordinating accessible dining and transportation under budget and consent constraints addresses a concrete, consequential multi-provider problem.
impact_evidence: Packet centers a wheelchair user’s dinner-and-ride need with a total budget constraint.
Claimed output includes exact prices, cancellation windows, and provider failure handling.
creativity_rationale: The neutral control plane, community connector foundry, live capability supply, and inspectable consent model are a memorable and ambitious WebMCP interaction design.
creativity_evidence: Missing restaurant capability is safely added through review and executable validation.
One approval governs a cross-provider outcome while preserving per-call provenance.
usability_note: The single-intent flow and explicit tool/call visibility are strong; multi-provider concepts may still be complex.
red_flags: Providers are synthetic fixtures, so real-world integration reliability is untested.
advance_reason: Top-tier leverage, impact, and creativity with a coherent demonstrated workflow.

one_line: A human-governed kitchen and bath co-design workspace with proposal hashes and evidence receipts.
what_it_does: Allows agents to inspect plans, search products, evaluate constraints, propose changes, and generate BOMs while reserving approval and consequential actions for humans.
leverage_rationale: Shared design state, bounded proposals, canonical-hash approval, and evidence receipts make consequential agent collaboration materially safer and more precise than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Packet describes state-aware tools, versioned proposals, exact-content hash binding, human-only approval, and receipts.
Frame sheet shows the Handshake concept and consent/problem framing, but not the live design workspace or tool calls.
execution_rationale: The stated workflow is unusually complete and intentional, but the viewed video evidence is mostly talking-head and slides rather than end-to-end product interaction.
execution_evidence: Packet reports an alive demo and enumerates design, constraint, approval, and receipt flows.
Frame sheet visibly confirms the product thesis and consent model but not operational completion.
impact_rationale: Kitchen and bath design has real cost, accessibility, geometry, and usability consequences; a reviewable co-design workflow can provide credible value to homeowners and designers.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies concrete planning risks and a synthetic catalog/constraint evaluation flow.
Slides explicitly frame agentic design consent and proof as the problem.
creativity_rationale: Binding approval to canonical proposal contents and producing proof receipts is a strong, original interaction model for design agents.
creativity_evidence: Tagline and slide concept center design together with approval proof.
Human-only checkpoints and absent irreversible tools are deliberate product architecture.
usability_note: The governance model is clear conceptually; live UI usability is under-evidenced in the video.
red_flags: Video is dominated by presentation material and does not visibly demonstrate the live workflow.
standouts: Evidence receipts and human-only consequential actions
advance_reason: Strong safety-centered concept, though execution confidence is reduced by thin product-motion evidence.

one_line: A municipal waste-rule interface that lets agents interpret items while humans retain disposal control.
what_it_does: Resolves indirect item descriptions, retrieves city-declared disposal rules, prepares eligible bulky-waste requests, and blocks unsafe items for manual review.
leverage_rationale: Structured municipality-declared rules reduce agent guessing and separate interpretation from authoritative decisions; ordinary UI automation could retrieve the same small set of results but with less reliable semantics and safety boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies resolve_item, get_disposal_rule, and prepare_bulky_pickup tools with a human confirmation gate.
Frame sheet shows the natural-language-to-municipal-rule UI and separated decision/interpretation sections.
execution_rationale: The static demo presents a coherent flow from indirect request through classification, fee calculation, and manual-review refusal, with concrete described tool-call counts.
execution_evidence: Packet reports eight WebMCP calls and an 800-yen confirmation total, while refusing a high-risk power bank.
Frame sheet visibly shows polished hero, test-rule, and structured-result states.
impact_rationale: Residents face genuinely confusing municipality-specific waste rules, and the product directly addresses ambiguity while preventing unsafe automated disposal actions.
impact_evidence: Packet explains differing rules by city, quantity, size, material, and safety risk.
Visible result distinguishes official municipal decision from agent interpretation.
creativity_rationale: The indirect-language interpretation plus municipal authority and human safety gate is a fresh, well-focused application of WebMCP, though the underlying lookup category is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Same item/different city framing is clear and memorable.
High-risk item refusal and preparation-without-finalization are thoughtful interaction choices.
usability_note: The staged answer and explicit decision/interpretation separation support understandable use.
red_flags: Municipality rules are fictional test data, so real-world authority is not demonstrated.
standouts: Safety refusal and human confirmation gate
advance_reason: Focused, credible civic utility with strong execution and safety design.

one_line: A deterministic WebMCP fault-injection demo that verifies authoritative state after reported tool success.
what_it_does: Runs a reservation action that falsely reports success, independently checks application state, and surfaces the resulting divergence.
leverage_rationale: Independent post-action state verification addresses a core limitation of trusting tool responses and is difficult to achieve reliably through generic UI driving alone.
leverage_evidence: Packet specifies reserve_table returning SUCCESS while persistence is absent, followed by authoritative lookup and divergence detection.
Frame sheet shows Runtime Truth states and a detected-status result, though no readable tool trace.
execution_rationale: The deterministic failure scenario is focused and coherent, but the frame sheet’s visible status is not enough to prove the complete declared-versus-observed comparison in detail.
execution_evidence: Packet gives a reproducible execution sequence and reports an alive implementation source stack.
Frames show the Runtime Truth application progressing to a visible detected status.
impact_rationale: Detecting false success is highly valuable for agents taking reservations, purchases, and other state-changing actions where silent divergence can cause real harm.
impact_evidence: Packet explicitly connects the problem to booking, buying, submitting, and changing application state.
The demo exposes a concrete false-success failure mode.
creativity_rationale: The narrow but important inversion—verify state rather than trust the tool response—is an original reliability interaction and a memorable demo premise.
creativity_evidence: Deterministic fault injection makes the reliability failure repeatable.
Declared result and authoritative state are explicitly compared as separate evidence.
usability_note: The concept is simple and legible, though the captured UI is sparse and technical details are small.
red_flags: The frame sheet does not visibly expose the full SUCCESS/NOT FOUND text at readable scale.
standouts: Reproducible fault injection for agent reliability
advance_reason: Important foundational reliability pattern with a focused demonstrated failure case.

one_line: A 3D dungeon for two players: a human explores while an AI co-game-master changes the world through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Provides exploration, combat, progression, and eight agent tools that read state, heal, open walls, place traps, spawn enemies, narrate floors, and run studies.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent direct, structured authority over live game state and world geometry, enabling a responsive co-game-master role that UI automation would reproduce unreliably.
leverage_evidence: Packet enumerates eight tools with real effects on HUD, walls, traps, enemies, and narration.
Frame sheet visibly shows gameplay, dialogue, and a portal/event state, though not an agent call trace.
execution_rationale: The playable 3D game appears visually coherent with HUD, character, dialogue, and world-event states; the packet describes a substantial five-floor scope, though agent-driven completion is not directly shown.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows consistent rendered dungeon scenes with HUD, dialogue, and a changing glowing world event.
Demo is alive and packet describes combat, leveling, and live tool effects.
impact_rationale: The target audience is players seeking emergent tabletop-like interaction, and an AI co-game-master can provide meaningful entertainment and replay value.
impact_evidence: Packet articulates the lost tabletop game-master dynamic and five-floor playable dungeon.
Visible game frames show a concrete playable world rather than a static pitch.
creativity_rationale: An AI co-game-master that modifies the actual 3D dungeon while enforcing progression rules is a highly memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The agent opens walls, sets traps, and summons real enemies instead of merely narrating.
The strength-is-unlocked design constraint gives the agent role depth.
usability_note: The game HUD and event feedback are visible; co-game-master interaction details are not directly captured.
red_flags: Video frames show gameplay events but no visible agent/tool invocation.
standouts: Direct world-changing tool effects with player-visible feedback
advance_reason: Exceptional creativity and strong product evidence for a genuinely agent-native game interaction.

one_line: A WebMCP workshop that preserves missing proof, bounded next actions, and human checkpoints for interrupted solo builders.
what_it_does: Maintains live workshop state and lets agents inspect, stop, draft unsigned plans, and return claimed work while reserving signature, verification, publication, and submission for humans.
leverage_rationale: State-aware bounded transitions and explicit absence of human-only actions give agents a safer, more reliable collaboration contract than DOM automation can provide.
leverage_evidence: Packet defines inspect_workshop, call_fermo, propose_workshop_draft, and return_work_result with state-aware permissions.
Frame sheet shows branded workshop/contract screens and progress-like workflow states, but no readable tool call.
execution_rationale: The workflow is carefully specified and visually coherent, but the video mainly shows document/workshop screens rather than an end-to-end interrupted-work recovery with evidence verification.
execution_evidence: Packet gives a concrete MANCA → draft → FIRMA → work → CLAIMED → VERIFIED flow.
Frame sheet shows multiple consistent contract/delivery and status screens.
impact_rationale: Interrupted solo builders have a real coordination and evidence problem, and preserving next action plus verification status can reduce lost context and false completion.
impact_evidence: Packet identifies interruption recovery, missing proof, and human checkpoints as the target needs.
Visible product screens show structured contract/delivery prompts and status information.
creativity_rationale: Treating unfinished work and missing proof as first-class state, with an explicit stop tool and human-only verification, is a novel workflow concept.
creativity_evidence: The MANCA concept and CLAIMED-versus-VERIFIED distinction are distinctive.
Tool surface deliberately excludes signature, publication, and final submission.
usability_note: The state model is thoughtful but the dense multilingual contract UI may require orientation.
red_flags: No direct visible tool invocation or evidence-verification completion in the frame sheet.
advance_reason: Strong workflow originality and practical solo-builder value, with moderate execution evidence limits.
